purpose: Remdesivir is used to treat COVID-19 in adults and children who are sick enough to need hospital care. It may also be used in some high-risk patients who do not need to be hospitalized. It helps your body fight the COVID-19 virus so you can recover faster.
how_it_works: The COVID-19 virus needs to make copies of itself inside your body to keep making you sick. Remdesivir works by sneaking into the virus and blocking the tool it uses to copy itself. When the virus cannot make copies, it stops spreading and your immune system has a better chance to fight it off.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is nausea. Some people also notice their liver enzymes go up, which your doctor will watch with blood tests. You might also feel a brief reaction during the IV infusion, such as sweating, shivering, or a faster heartbeat.
warnings: Remdesivir is given through an IV in a hospital or clinic setting, so medical staff will watch you closely. Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as this may affect whether you can take it. It is not recommended during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk, so always let your doctor know if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Some people have had serious allergic reactions, so staff will monitor you during and after the infusion.
typical_dosing: For most adults and children, Remdesivir is given as a once-daily IV infusion over about 30 to 120 minutes. Hospitalized patients usually receive a 200 mg loading dose on Day 1, followed by 100 mg once daily for up to 5 to 10 days depending on how sick they are. Non-hospitalized high-risk patients typically receive 3 days of treatment. Your doctor will decide the exact schedule that is right for you.
